review: 1:1–1:2 רֹאשׁ / וּמְלֹאוֹ — Eph 1:23 (הַמְּלֵאָה, 'the fullness'); the Arabic رَأْسٌ وَمِلْؤُهُ is that verse, and the Hebrew keeps the head/body image without adding 'the church'.

2:2 כִּמְבַשֵּׂר — 'as one announcing good news', for كَسَابِقٍ ('forerunner'); the Greek πρόδρομος behind the Arabic is 'forerunner', and Hebrew has no noun for it, so the participle carries the sense of going ahead to announce.
3:3 וּכְצֶלֶם הַנֶּאֱמָן — 'and after the image of the Faithful One'; the Arabic صُورَةِ الْأَمِين is 2 Cor 3:18 / Rom 8:29, and צֶלֶם is the Genesis word for image.
4:3 עַד נִרְאֵהוּ בְּעַיִן — 'until we see Him with the eye', for بِالْعِيَان; the phrase is the biblical 'eye to eye' (Isa 52:8) stripped to its shortest form for the metre.
